Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Horizon private offer — packaging constraints + channel margin needs

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and sourcing dug into the usage profile and we have two immediate asks before we can proceed to PO: one on packaging and one on channel economics.

1) Packaging: we need a single SKU that covers both inference and embedding usage for our clinical insights team. They want a predictable per-month line item (not metered by token) up to a soft cap, with an overage path. This is to fit Horizon's internal chargeback model.

2) Channel margin: our reseller (RegionalHealth Distributors) requires a minimum 12% pass-through on list price to keep their margins and support managed deployment/ops. Horizon will only sign if that margin path is respected or otherwise compensated via invoice credits.

Can Redwood propose a clean private-offer layout that accomplishes the above (preferably a bundled SKU) and propose how you would route channel pass-through without breaking listprice commitments to your marketplace? Procurement also attached (see attached MA plan v3) the draft terms — we expect minor redlines.

Elena
Attachments: Horizon_MA_plan_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Nov 2025 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing guidance for Horizon private offer

Mina — pricing perspective: baseline economics for a HIPAA U.S. customer (private deployment, reasonable QPS) suggest we need at least a 20% gross margin on list to account for infra and support. If we must give the reseller a guaranteed 12% pass-through, that eats into margin. Two workable options:

Option A — Bundled fixed SKU (recommended if Horizon wants predictability). We set list price at $55k/month, give Horizon a committed discount to land at $45k/month (so effective Redwood net = $45k). We then pay RegionalHealth a 12% reseller fee (invoiced separately or via reseller line) — net to Redwood ≈ $39.6k before infra costs. This reduces gross margin but preserves listprice for marketplace reporting.

Option B — Anchor listprice up, but provide reseller with an uplift credit (one-time or quarterly true-up) instead of guaranteed monthly pass-through. Example: list $60k, Horizon pays $48k, and we issue RegionalHealth a quarterly rebate equal to 12% of list for tracked usage. That keeps our per-month cashflow healthier but requires a reconciliation process.

Operationally, Option B is preferable for margin protection; Option A is simpler for procurement. We can also propose a hybrid: a slightly higher list price + smaller direct pass-through + quarterly rebate floor.

Rishi
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

Subject: Private-offer options — Horizon packaging + channel margin (2 proposals attached)

Hi Elena / Markus,

Appreciate the clarity on Horizon's internal requirements — attached are two concrete private-offer structures for review:

- Proposal 1 (Procurement-simple): Bundled fixed SKU (monthly line item) that covers inference + embeddings up to a soft cap. List price $55k/mo, Horizon committed price $45k/mo. We will include a reseller pass-through fee of 12% of list as a separate invoice line payable to RegionalHealth. This keeps your internal chargeback model intact and requires minimal reconciliation on your side. See attached "privoffer_option_comparison.xlsx" for numbers and example invoice stubs.

- Proposal 2 (Margin-protected): Higher list price with quarterly reseller rebate. List price $60k/mo, Horizon net $48k/mo, with a quarterly reconciliation that pays RegionalHealth a 12% credit based on aggregated usage. This reduces monthly cash flow impact to Redwood and simplifies the reseller accounting on our end, but adds a quarterly reconciliation step for Horizon.

Attachments: privoffer_option_comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Ask: please confirm which option procurement prefers and whether the attached "procurement_terms_redline.pdf" contains any blocker redlines. If Horizon prefers Proposal 1, we can prepare a DocuSign package and a sample PO mapping to our AR team. If Proposal 2, we'll include reconciliation language and a quarterly true-up schedule.

Happy to jump on a quick call this week to walk through the invoice examples.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
